text:
infra-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx error rate for hosted-api in sfo1 (edge -> api-gateway). 60s error rate = 12.4% :rotating_light:

alice: seeing multiple customer escalations for timeouts and 502s around 09:12 PDT. example: curl to /v1/generate returns HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway quickly then connection reset.

maya: agreed. metrics: gateway lat p50 up 3x, p95 6x. egress packet loss to ISP-A for sfo1-edge1 is ~4-6% over last 10m on interface eth2.

ben: any BGP events? could be asymmetric route or multi-path split.

maya: yes, our bgp-monitor shows repeated next-hop changes for prefixes through ISP-A at 09:10:11 -> 09:11:05 -> 09:12:20. sample from collector: 
```
09:10:11 UPDATE prefix 203.0.113.0/24 NEXT_HOP 198.51.100.2
09:11:05 WITHDRAW prefix 203.0.113.0/24
09:12:20 ANNOUNCE prefix 203.0.113.0/24 NEXT_HOP 198.51.100.6
```

alice: tcpdump from sfo1-edge1 during spike shows lots of retransmits and dup ACKs to 203.0.113.0/24. pasted small snippet: 
```
09:11:43.123456 IP ourgw > 203.0.113.45: Flags [.], ack 1234, win 342, length 0
09:11:43.124001 IP 203.0.113.45 > ourgw: Flags [P.], seq 2345:2398, ack 1234, win 256, length 53
09:11:43.124500 IP ourgw > 203.0.113.45: Flags [F.], seq 1234, ack 2398, win 342, length 0
```

oncall-snow: I'm standing up a mitigation. first step: shift a percentage of traffic off sfo1-edge1 to sfo1-edge2 and route via ISP-B. prepping commands.

ben: +1. can we set gateway fallback to prefer nearby region euw1 for non-latency-sensitive background jobs? also enable edge-level retry to avoid 502 bubbling to customers.

maya: Carrier ops already pinged ISP-A NOC. they report a correlated fiber splice and are investigating a partial mux failure affecting multipath. carrier-ops: "we've opened a ticket, seeing flaps on egress bundle, pushing techs to site".

alice: repro steps for support: 
1) hit hosted API from a client in us-west -> see 502s within 10-30s bursts
2) `curl -v` shows TCP connection resets and downstream 502 from our gateway service
3) mtr to 203.0.113.45 shows packet loss starting at our peering hop

support-liaison: I'm pinging affected customers with an interim note: "We're investigating intermittent 5xx/timeouts in SFO region; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30m or on status.redwood.ai."

oncall-snow: mitigation actions executed: 
- reweighted edge LB: sfo1-edge1 20% -> sfo1-edge2 80%
- enabled short-retry (3 -> 5) on gateway route policy for sfo1 for 10m
- scaled edge proxy pool +2 instances in sfo1
Commands: 
```
# reweight
redwoodctl lb reweight --region sfo1 --from sfo1-edge1 --to sfo1-edge2 --percent 60
# set retry
redwoodctl gateway set-policy --region sfo1 --retry-count 5 --ttl 600
```

maya: after reweight, 5xx dropped from 12.4% -> 2.1% over 5m. packet loss on eth2 trending down to 1.2% but still noisy.

carrier-ops: ISP-A: "we've migrated traffic to alternate mux, expected stabilization in 20-40 minutes. will confirm BGP adj timeouts reduced."

ben: recommend follow-ups: run a canary for 1hr, schedule peering teams to review multipath hashing, add automated region-failover doc to runbook. also validate auth token replay behavior since retries might surface duplicate billing tokens.

alice: filed internal ticket RED-INC-2026 linking bgp logs, tcpdumps, and customer reports. tagging platform and billing teams for auth/billing review.

support-liaison: customer update posted to status: "Partial degradation in SFO affecting some customers; mitigation reduced errors — monitoring continues." :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: RESOLVED? automatic check in 30m. next update expected 09:55 PDT.

ben: thanks team. postmortem notes: consider adding egress path health probe that triggers auto-reweight when >2% loss for 5m.

maya: adding that to infra backlog.
